answer: The ocean hash-assigns every agent a duty quill each epoch, and an epoch signature is valid only over a ripple bought from that quill at its rung: the n-th purchase still on the quill's karst tally burns base×2^(n−1) of ocean. The karst never clears, and a purchase leaves the tally only when the epoch it bought is judged honest — fakes never are. So an operator's k clones, spread over P duty quills and any number of epochs, leave kt unstruck purchases and every clone's next ripple burns about base×2^(kt/P) of ocean. A newcomer whose epochs are judged honest strikes each one and pays base.
